title: Choose the studio's new visual world
question: Sage and black, quieter, same layout. The roll assigned The Order Book. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: The Order Book
options.lineage: a workshop's bound commission book and its sign-off stamps
options.thesis: Every idea is a numbered commission, signed off station by station by the crew who built it.
options.viewport: Office and Maya on top, the commission book and the open order below; each job wears its number and a row of crew stamps (Asha planned, Ben & Chloe built, Grace signed off).
options.risk: Becomes a ledger costume if ruled-paper texture creeps in; the stamps must stay clean marks, never clip-art.

raised.raise: Status is a mark in a fixed box: filled done, hollow waiting, struck through in red when blocked.
Hierarchy comes from type scale alone; no glows, gradients or ornament.
Areas divide by flat sage and black fields, never by shadow or glow.
The office screen owns its panel edge to edge.

options.label: The Job Traveller
options.lineage: the shop-floor card that travels with a job and is stamped at each station
options.thesis: One card rides with each job through plan, build, check and final check, stamped at every station.
options.viewport: The start card becomes a tall traveller with five station boxes; project cards carry their last stamp.
options.risk: Familiar: it sits close to the five-step progress tracker most build tools ship.

options.label: Boarding Pass & Gate Board
options.lineage: airline boarding passes and departure boards
options.thesis: Projects are passes; the current run is a board row that holds its alert until you have noticed.
options.viewport: Projects as segmented passes with tabular figures; the run reads as one board row with its state cell.
options.case: Fuses cleanly and reads fast; loses on identification: a trip, not a workshop crew.
options.risk: Travel metaphors can feel borrowed when the board has only one row.

options.label: Black Console
options.thesis: A black working surface split by hairline seams, sage only where state lives.
options.viewport: Black ground, panels tiled and seamed, sage reserved for selection and live state.
options.case: Clear as a working tool; loses on identification: it is the default AI-tool look the studio is leaving.
options.risk: Drifts back to the glowing dark-dashboard rut the detector just flagged.

options.label: Timetable Slide Rack
options.thesis: One type size; rank by weight, case and reversal.
options.viewport: Raked slides of runs along one lit bed.
options.case: Raked containers fight a working screen.
options.risk: Unreadable at a glance for a tool.
options.kept: Status as a mark in a fixed box: filled, hollow, struck.

options.label: Type Specimen
options.viewport: One giant glyph and a breathing grid.
options.case: Nothing in it is about building with a team.
options.kept: Hierarchy by type scale alone, no ornament.

options.label: Zoo Guide Map
options.thesis: Flat colour lobes do all the dividing.
options.case: Overshoot motion and lobes cost task clarity.
options.risk: Playful at the expense of status.
options.kept: Divide areas with flat colour fields, never shadow.

options.label: Vertical Feed
options.thesis: One item owns the whole frame.
options.viewport: One project fills the screen at a time.
options.case: Breaks the four-area layout you asked to keep.
options.kept: The office screen owns its panel edge to edge.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean app dashboard in sage and black, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: The arrangement a returning user expects, at full craft.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from other tools by design.
